question: Can the 50 in-scope PDFs yield a usable text layer without OCR, and on what calibration constants?

verdict.one_line: 48/50 yield a trustworthy text layer, 2 are sparse books with real characters on mostly-image pages, and ZERO require OCR. No OCR tooling is needed, approved, or bought.

extractor.provenance: Ubuntu 24.04 universe package python3-pypdf 4.0.2-1, installed via apt. NOT a pip download, NOT a vendor product, no account, no egress.
extractor.rule_2: intact. Rule 2 forbids paid tiers, metered APIs, and vendor free-credit tiers. A distro package is none of those.
extractor.route: page.extract_text(visitor_text=...) reading per-span font size, baseline and x
extractor.route_rejected: content-stream Tj/TJ regex. Yields hex glyph indices, not characters. Measured, not assumed: see self_correction_1.
extractor.images: ENUMERATED via /Resources /XObject, never decoded. 0 image bytes written across the whole run.

calibration_remeasured.method: Every constant re-measured on this corpus. The course-corpus-extraction skill's values were measured on FireShot-captured web pages; its own rule is to re-measure before relying on them.

y_tol.stability_test: SHA-256 of the ordered non-empty line TEXTS at Y_TOL 0.0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.6 / 1.0 / 2.0 / 3.0 / 5.0 pt
y_tol.result: byte-identical on 48 of 50 documents across the entire band
y_tol.geometry_moves_baselines: 444 -> 128 on the 22-page Swipe document; the TEXT does not move
y_tol.load_bearing_note: On these 2 the digest differs across the band. Their baselines sit within a few points of each other, so 0.6 is a real choice there, not a free one. Both are 1.0pt documents. Recorded as a known non-uniformity, not smoothed over.

tier_min.rule: raster/sparse gate first; then title = largest tier, body = most frequent tier, every OTHER tier = a heading tier
tier_min.sensitivity: populations on the 22-page document are 395 / 133 / 11. T in 2..10 all recover the same tiers. T=5 chosen to tolerate a stray span that T=2 would promote to a tier.
tier_min.measured_on_corpus: Swipe.pdf -> title 60.0pt, headings [24.0pt] over 133 lines (25% of 539), body 11.04pt

constants_rejected.skill_flat_18.0pt: wrong here. This corpus tiers 60 / 24 / 11.04. A flat 18.0 sits between the body and the heading and would work by luck, not by measurement.
constants_rejected.title_size_times_0.55: wrong here, and it fails SILENTLY. 60 * 0.55 = 33.0pt, which excludes the 24.0pt tier. This is what made the first extractor classify all 3 documents title_only.

classification_taxonomy.note: Three classes, not two. A binary text/raster gate was tried first and discarded: it classified 7 readable documents as degenerate and would have discarded real characters.
classification_taxonomy.text: trustworthy layout. Tiering and reflow valid. 48 documents.
classification_taxonomy.sparse: real characters, mostly-image pages. Text extracted, layout flagged untrusted, never silently dropped. 2 documents: '2. AC eBook' and 'AC_Book', both 340 pages at 3.4-3.5 words/page with 0.18 images/page. 1,372 words combined.
classification_taxonomy.raster: no recoverable characters. Would require OCR. 0 documents.

safety_invariants_held.token_multiset_preserved: true on every audited document. content_tokens(text_in) == content_tokens(text_out), asserted over whitespace-split tokens so the single permitted edit (one inserted space at a join) is blind to it.
safety_invariants_held.chars_stripped_equal: true on every audited document. No character added, dropped, or altered by reflow.

link_layer.rule: /Annots is the ONLY authoritative link layer.
link_layer.evidence: Swipe.pdf carries 400 raw annotations of which 201 are distinct - exactly half are boilerplate repeats. The text layer's copy of those URLs is MANGLED by line wrapping: a Google Sheets link renders as '...acQ/e' then 'dit#gid=5683798' on the next baseline, and the word 'Calculator' is torn to 'Calcu' / 'dit#gid=...' / 'lator'.
link_layer.consequence: Display text must never be used to recover a URL. Read annots.

self_corrections.claim_withdrawn: '4/4 PDFs have a text layer; zero image-only.'
self_corrections.why_wrong: The test counted raw content-stream bytes as characters. Hex glyph indices are bytes, so a raster page with a degenerate font produced 449,418 apparent 'characters' and 597/597 'pages with text'.
self_corrections.truth: The 597-page document is not a clean text layer. It reports a genuine 1.0pt dominant font. Separately it does yield 101 words/page, so its characters are recoverable while its layout is not.
self_corrections.lesson: Character count is not a text-layer test. A hex-index stream produces plenty of bytes.

self_corrections.why_wrong: Printed 539 lines at every Y_TOL while distinct baselines fell 444 -> 128. Those cannot both describe one grouping. The counter measured document-wide distinct y, which repeats per page, so it could not have failed.
self_corrections.truth: Stability IS real, and now proven by text digest rather than by a count that cannot fail.
self_corrections.lesson: Same class as the fetch probe: a zero that evaluates nothing.

self_corrections.claim_withdrawn: 'The 1.0pt reading is probably my own fallback value, contaminating the gate.'
self_corrections.why_wrong: Hypothesised, then measured. fallback_share = 0.0% on all documents: pypdf reports font_size=1.0 directly and the tm[5] fallback never fires.
self_corrections.truth: 1.0pt is a real reported font size on 7 documents. The gate was not contaminated; the documents genuinely are typeset at an unusable size.
self_corrections.lesson: A hypothesis about one's own code is not a finding until instrumented. This one survived contact with the instrument.

self_corrections.claim_withdrawn: n/a - operational defect, not a claim
self_corrections.why_wrong: The first fetch probe reported 4/4 FAILURES while the route was working perfectly. mega-get names its output after the VERBATIM source file and appends the extension ('Vimeo gif thumbnail custom code.pdf'); the matcher looked for '<handle>.pdf'.
self_corrections.truth: Fixed by fetching into an empty per-handle directory and taking whatever single file lands. No name matching at all.
self_corrections.lesson: Never infer fetch failure from the absence of an expected filename.

instruments_discarded.max_spans_per_line_as_merge_detector: The 22-page document legitimately places 48 kerning runs on one baseline. Span count cannot distinguish that from a baseline merge. Replaced by the text digest.
instruments_discarded.document_wide_distinct_y_as_baseline_cou: Floating-point noise inflates it and y repeats per page, so it can never equal line count. Removed from the stability test entirely.

cost.bandwidth: 0.159 GB fetched per-file over the solved route, plus apt packages from the Ubuntu archive
cost.vm_changes: python3-pypdf 4.0.2 installed. Nothing else added. No pip, no venv, no account, no key.
cost.transferable_to_the_operator_pc: nothing. Every byte of this ran on the VM.

plan_impact.synthesis_section_7: The plan's PDF gate said '~25 of 50 may be image-only, measured not assumed, empty_extraction never OCR-billed.' The measurement is done: the suspicion was wrong. 0 need OCR. The gate simplifies from a probe-gate to a three-class classifier with the sparse branch carrying 2 documents and 1,372 words.
plan_impact.written_hand_completeness: All 50 PDFs are accounted for. None is lost, stubbed, or dropped. 109 documents = 37 written_hand + 36 course_doc + 36 orphan, of which 50 are PDFs and 59 are docx/pptx/xlsx.
plan_impact.w0_pdf_gate: SATISFIED. May be closed rather than carried as an open probe.

open: 1.0pt documents: characters extract, layout does not. Whether the vault needs their layout at all is a presentation decision, not an extraction one. Flagged, not decided.

2 documents (AC eBook, AC_Book) are 340-page image books at 3.4 words/page. Their 1,372 words are the whole recoverable text. Anything else in them is pixels and would need OCR that is not approved. Recorded as a completeness limit on those 2 documents only.

'7-Figure VSL Script Template' was classified degenerate in the ceiling run but missed by the fallback audit on a name mismatch. Its ceiling-run measurement was 814 words/page, 80x the sparse threshold, so it is readable by the same metric. Not separately audited.
